title: Callsmith Provider Pack
description: Each provider declares its real audio/transport/lifecycle contract plus known potholes. The resolver reconciles these across the selected stack to produce the compatibility matrix and audio bridge contract. This file documents the shape every providers/*/<id>.json must follow.

id.description: Stable identifier, matches menu option id. Lowercase-kebab.

directions.description: Which call directions this provider supports. Used for surface/direction impossibility detection.

native_capabilities.description: Native capabilities that short-circuit the resolver (e.g. audio_normalization absorbs the decode/resample bridge).

ingest.description: The audio format this component needs to RECEIVE on its input side (what the bridge must hand it).

egress.description: The audio format this component PRODUCES on its output side (what the bridge receives from it).

model.description: Current verified model ID. Pinned by staleness guard tests.

streaming.description: Whether this provider supports streaming output.

tool_calling.description: Whether this provider supports function/tool calling.

context_window.description: Maximum context window in tokens (LLM only).

latency_estimates.description: Typical latency contribution from this provider in milliseconds. Used for latency budget computation.

ttfa_ms.description: TTS: time to first audio chunk.

response_start_ms.description: Realtime model: time to first audio response.

interruption.description: How this provider participates in barge-in / interruption handling.

mechanism.description: The interruption mechanism this provider uses.

description.description: What happens when the user interrupts.

lifecycle.description: Session/call lifecycle events this provider emits or expects.

cost_estimates.description: Pricing data for cost estimation. per_minute_usd is pre-normalized for the resolver to sum.

rate_usd.description: Raw rate in the billing unit.

per_minute_usd.description: Normalized cost per minute (USD). Pre-computed from billing + rate using conversational assumptions.
